/-- **The χ-ledger, closed** (★): for every Weil divisor `D` on the curve bundle,
`χ(𝒪(D)) = χ(𝒪_X) + deg D`. Base case `𝒪(0) ≅ 𝒪_X`, step `chi_step`, glue
`CurveDivisor.induction_devissage`. -/
theorem chi_divisorSheaf (D : X.CurveDivisor) :
    Sheaf.chi (X.divisorSheaf K D) =
      Sheaf.chi (X.moduleKSheaf K) + CurveDivisor.deg K D := by
  refine Scheme.CurveDivisor.induction_devissage
    (P := fun D => Sheaf.chi (X.divisorSheaf K D) =
      Sheaf.chi (X.moduleKSheaf K) + CurveDivisor.deg K D)
    ?_ (fun {x} hx D => ?_) D
  · rw [Sheaf.chi_congr (divisorSheafZeroIso K), CurveDivisor.deg_zero, add_zero]
  · rw [devissageDivisor_eq_sub hx D]
    have hstep := chi_step K hx D
    have hdeg := deg_devissageDivisor K hx D
    rw [devissageDivisor_eq_sub hx D] at hdeg
    constructor <;> intro h <;> omega

/-- **Principal divisors have degree zero**: `deg (div g) = 0` for a unit `g` of the
function field. Multiplication by `g` identifies `𝒪(0)` with `𝒪(0 − div g)`
(`mulEquivDivisorSheaf`), so the two sides of the χ-ledger force the degrees to agree. -/
theorem deg_divOf (g : X.functionFieldˣ) :
    CurveDivisor.deg K (Scheme.divOf (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) g) = 0 := by
  have hcongr := Sheaf.chi_congr (mulEquivDivisorSheaf K g (0 : X.CurveDivisor))
  rw [chi_divisorSheaf K (0 : X.CurveDivisor),
    chi_divisorSheaf K ((0 : X.CurveDivisor) - Scheme.divOf (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) g),
    CurveDivisor.deg_zero, zero_sub, CurveDivisor.deg_neg] at hcongr
  omega

/-- **The Riemann inequality** (G9, general conditional form): for every Weil divisor `D`,
`deg D + χ(𝒪_X) ≤ h⁰(𝒪(D))` — from the χ-ledger and `h¹ ≥ 0`. The curve-level
`deg D + 1 − genus` form is derived in `ChiCurve`. -/
theorem riemann_inequality (D : X.CurveDivisor) :
    CurveDivisor.deg K D + Sheaf.chi (X.moduleKSheaf K) ≤
      (Sheaf.h0 (X.divisorSheaf K D) : ℤ) := by
  have h := chi_divisorSheaf K D
  have hchi : Sheaf.chi (X.divisorSheaf K D) ≤ (Sheaf.h0 (X.divisorSheaf K D) : ℤ) := by
    rw [Sheaf.chi]
    omega
  omega

/-- **Unbounded growth of `h⁰` along multiples of a point** (G9): for every closed point
`x` and every bound `N` there is `n` with `N ≤ h⁰(𝒪(n · x))`. No rational point is
needed: `residueDeg x ≥ 1` suffices. -/
theorem h0_nsmul_point_unbounded {x : X} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X) (N : ℕ) :
    ∃ n : ℕ, N ≤ Sheaf.h0 (X.divisorSheaf K (n • CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) := by
  have key : ∀ n : ℕ, (n : ℤ) - Sheaf.h1 (X.moduleKSheaf K) ≤
      (Sheaf.h0 (X.divisorSheaf K (n • CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) : ℤ) := by
    intro n
    have hchi := chi_divisorSheaf K (n • CurveDivisor.single hx 1)
    rw [Scheme.CurveDivisor.nsmul_single_one hx n,
      Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg_single' K hx (n : ℤ)] at hchi
    have hchile : Sheaf.chi (X.divisorSheaf K (n • CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) ≤
        (Sheaf.h0 (X.divisorSheaf K (n • CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) : ℤ) := by
      rw [Sheaf.chi]
      omega
    have hres : (1 : ℤ) ≤ (X.residueDeg K x : ℤ) := by
      exact_mod_cast Scheme.residueDeg_pos hx
    have hmul : (n : ℤ) * 1 ≤ (n : ℤ) * (X.residueDeg K x : ℤ) :=
      mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hres (by positivity)
    have hchiO : Sheaf.chi (X.moduleKSheaf K) =
        (Sheaf.h0 (X.moduleKSheaf K) : ℤ) - Sheaf.h1 (X.moduleKSheaf K) := rfl
    -- `hchi` rewrote the divisor to `single hx n`; transport back is definitional
    have hchi' : Sheaf.chi (X.divisorSheaf K (n • CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) =
        Sheaf.chi (X.moduleKSheaf K) + (n : ℤ) * (X.residueDeg K x : ℤ) := by
      rw [Scheme.CurveDivisor.nsmul_single_one hx n]

---
name: private-hides-the-name-not-the-proof
description: A `private` mathlib lemma is not a wall — its proof may use only public API, so re-derive it instead of pricing an upstream PR.
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

When a mathlib lemma you need is `private`, check whether its **proof** uses only public
API before concluding you cannot have it. `private` restricts the *name*, not the argument.

Established 2026-07-28 (AJC run 0067, `ajc-pic0av`). `AlgebraicGeometry.smooth_of_grpObj`
requires `GeometricallyReduced` (every field base change); internally it reduces to
reducedness over one algebraic closure, but through
`private smooth_of_grpObj_of_isAlgClosed`. Two independent projects each concluded the cheap
route was **an upstream PR making it public**, and recorded that as the wall. It wasn't: the
proof uses only public API (`smoothLocus_eq_top_iff`, `dense_smoothLocus_of_perfectField`,
`preimage_smoothLocus_eq`, `nonempty_inter_closedPoints`, `pointEquivClosedPoint`,
`GrpObj.mulRight`, `LocallyOfFiniteType.jacobsonSpace`). Transcribed verbatim into the
project — same `set_option`s, same `open`s — it elaborated with zero errors on the first try.

**Why:** the value is not the transcription, it's that the reduction was *strict*. The
re-derived form takes `IsReduced` of one scheme where the public form takes a class
quantifying over all field extensions, and the converse implication is genuinely absent from
mathlib. So the "wall" was an artefact of which intermediate statement happened to be
exported.

**How to apply:** read the private proof's tactic script and check each name's visibility
before pricing an upstream PR or a local re-proof from scratch. Attribute the mathematics to
the original author in the docstring and say why you re-derived rather than imported. Then
measure with a probe *and* a control ([[axiom-probe-with-control]]) — a reduction is worth
nothing until something measures it.

The general form, from `ajc-fbc` hitting it independently the same day on flat exactness (no
visibility issue at all): **the frontier is often an artefact of how strongly the obligation
was stated.** An obligation gets phrased at the strongest generality that keeps the sentence
true, that phrasing becomes the wall, and the consumer only ever instantiates it somewhere
weaker. Related: [[port-the-idea-not-the-proof]], [[search-object-shape-not-argument-shape]].

---
name: route-can-be-over-strong-too
description: When a source proof's route needs vocabulary mathlib lacks, look for a different criterion for the same conclusion — properness via the valuative criterion, not quasi-projectivity.
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

An obligation can be walled by its **route** rather than by its hypotheses. When the textbook
proof needs vocabulary the library does not have, the question to ask is *what does the
conclusion need*, not *how did the source prove it*.

Established 2026-07-28 (AJC run 0067, `ajc-pic0av`). Properness of `Pic⁰_{C/k}` had a standing
caveat: Kleiman §5 argues through **quasi-projectivity**, and mathlib v4.31 has no
quasi-projectivity API at all. The project had carried that as the blocker for many sessions
and expected to route around it by base change to `k̄`. But properness has another standard
criterion — the **valuative criterion** (Stacks 01KF), which mathlib ships as
`UniversallyClosed.of_valuativeCriterion` / `IsProper.eq_valuativeCriterion`. Against it the
residue became a *lifting* statement, and the other three conjuncts of `IsProper` were already
theorems in the file — including a `QuasiCompact` lemma whose docstring said it was "not needed
for the `proper` assembly", which is exactly what the new route consumes.

**Why:** a missing-vocabulary blocker reads like a hard mathematical wall and is recorded as
one, but it is a statement about the *library*, not about the theorem. Different criteria for
the same conclusion have different vocabulary needs, and the reduction that lands is the one
whose hypothesis the library can even express.

**How to apply:** when a docstring blames missing library vocabulary, enumerate the *other*
standard criteria for that conclusion and check which mathlib has. Then check what the new
route's side conditions are — they are often already proved and filed as "not needed".
Also worth checking whether the reduction improves the *shape*: here, representability turns
valuative lifting into "an invertible sheaf on `C ×_k Spec K` extends over the valuation
ring", the same species of extension statement as the chapter's own square-zero results.

Sibling failure mode, same day, opposite direction:
[[private-hides-the-name-not-the-proof]] — there the *hypothesis* was over-strong.
